glosses: To form (something) by combining materials or parts.

examples.text: It was a bridge ybuilt in goodly wize, / With curious Corbes and pendants grauen faire, [...]

Athelstan Arundel walked home all the way, foaming and raging. No omnibus, cab, or conveyance ever built could contain a young man in such a rage. His mother lived at Pembridge Square, which is four good measured miles from Lincoln's Inn.
A chap named Eleazir Kendrick and I had chummed in together the summer afore and built a fish-weir and shanty at Setuckit Point, down Orham way. For a spell we done pretty well.

glosses: To develop or give form to (something) according to a plan or process.

examples.text: The dirty secret of the internet is that all this distraction and interruption is immensely profitable. Web companies like to boast about […], or offering services that let you [...] "share the things you love with the world" and so on. But the real way to build a successful online business is to be better than your rivals at undermining people's control of their own attention.

glosses: To increase or strengthen (something) by adding gradually to.

examples.text: Since the launch early last year of […] two Silicon Valley start-ups offering free education through MOOCs, massive open online courses, the ivory towers of academia have been shaken to their foundations. University brands built in some cases over centuries have been forced to contemplate the possibility that information technology will rapidly make their existing business model obsolete.

glosses: To establish a basis for (something).
To form by combining materials or parts.
To develop in magnitude or extent.
To construct (software) by compiling its source code.
To be converted into software by compilation, usually with minimal human intervention.

examples.text: This code won’t build any more. Have you made any changes?

glosses: The physique of a human or animal body, or other object; constitution or structure.

examples.text: Rugby players are of sturdy build.
According to the prevailing adolescent criteria Roger was not good looking. He had no build and did not give off very assertive, let alone aggressive vibrations.

glosses: Any of various versions of a software product as it is being developed for release to users.

examples.text: The computer company has introduced a new prototype build to beta testers.

glosses: The process or period of constructing a physical object.

examples.text: This new Lego set was a very nice build.

glosses: A structure, such as a building, statue, pool or forest created by the player.

examples.text: I made a build that looked like the Parthenon in that game.

glosses: A configuration of a character's items or skills created by the player.

examples.text: I made a build centered around attack speed.

In fact, thousands of D&D players constantly debate the virtues of various character builds (combinations of race, class, feat, and spell choices) and share their efforts with each other in hundreds of message boards and mailing lists.

glosses: Something constructed from parts.

examples.text: The artwork was a construct of wire and tubes.
Loops and conditional statements are constructs in computer programming.

glosses: A concept or model.

examples.text: Bohr's theoretical construct of the atom was soon superseded by quantum mechanics.

glosses: A segment of nucleic acid, created artificially, for transplantation into a target cell or tissue.
To build or form (something) by assembling parts.

examples.text: We constructed the radio from spares.
A wall constructed of random stones.

glosses: To build (a sentence, an argument, etc.) by arranging words or ideas.

examples.text: A sentence may be constructed with a subject, verb and object.
The Vietnam War films are forms of memory that function to provide collective rememberings, to construct history, and to subsume within them the experience of the veterans.

glosses: To draw (a geometric figure) by following precise specifications and using geometric tools and techniques.

examples.text: Construct a circle that touches each vertex of the given triangle.
